An Erasmus Mundus scholarship will be available only to a percentage of those places.For non-scholarship holders, tuition fees for the whole study period of four semesters are to be paid in two instalments – half before the beginning of the first semester and half before the beginning of the third semester. Tuition fees Students from EU/EEA: €2,000 per academic yearStudents from outside EU/EEA: €4,000 per academic year The tuition fees include Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders do not have to pay participation costs or tuition fees. Participation in all classes offered within the SSI2 curriculum, including the prep-camp, Winter School and Summer School.Emergency and accident insurance according to the minimum requirements of the Erasmus+ Programme.Support with administrative and organisational issues by the consortium partners.Costs for enrolment at the institutions of the consortium partners.All examinations.Issuing of the final diploma. sourceFacts.fundingTerms1: Costs & Funding ​Home > Applications > Costs and Funding 4500 € per semester Participation Costs Currently, the Consortium charges the following participation costs to be paid to the consortium: ​ ​ ​ The participation costs cover all obligatory programme activities and health insurance; they do also include the respective hosting university's obligatory registration and student service fees. They do not include room and board as well as other living expenses and travel. For required travel read more about our mobility path. ​ There are three funding options for students. Your choice needs to be be specified in the application but does NOT need to be justified, nor will it affect how your application is rated. ​ Funding optionsErasmus+ Scholarship HoldersThe Erasmus+ Scholarship holders are selected based on merit. They will receive a monthly scholarship of 1400€ for 24 months plus their health insurance, university registration and student service fees will be covered. Scholarship holders are required to cover the cost of mobility (e.g. travel, visa, vaccinations, residence permit fees) according to the obligatory EMMIR mobility path from their monthly stipends. There are no additional payments for travel and installation. ​​​​Non-Fee Paying Self-Funded StudentsThe non-fee paying self-funded students are also selected based on merit. They will not have to pay participation cost and their health insurance, university registration and student service fees will be covered. They will have to cover their living cost incl. travel costs according to the obligatory EMMIR mobility path. When applying for the student visa, non-fee paying students will have to prove that they have the financial means to cover their living cost for the two-year-study programme including the mobility path.Fee-Paying Self-Funded StudentsThe fee-paying self-funded students are required to pay 4500€ participation cost per semester plus their living expenses including travel costs according to the obligatory EMMIR mobility path. Their health insurance, university registration and student service fees will be covered by the participation costs. When applying for the student visa, fee-paying self-funded students will have to prove that they have the financial means to cover their participation and living cost for the two-year-study programme including the mobility path.​Erasmus+ Scholarships When applying for EMMIR, applicants are invited to apply for one of a very limited number of Erasmus+ scholarships (except if they have benefitted from such a scholarship before). Applicants will be informed if they are awarded a scholarship with the admission notification. Please note that you can only apply for a scholarship if you have completed a first degree (i.a.w. if you are able to document a finalised degree) by the application deadline in 20 December 2026. No exceptions can be made from this rule. ​ Applications for Erasmus Mundus scholarships will be open until 20 December 2026 for the 2027-29 edition. Please see visit this page for further information about deadlines of applications. For non-fee paying self-funded students the deadline 20 December also applies, the admission period for fee-paying self-funded students closes at latest on 15 July 2027 (depending on the availability of study places). ​ Other Scholarships, Loans and Third Party Grants Inform yourself about funding opportunities in your country. Our team will (after you have received your notification letter) provide you with documents you might need from EMMIR. ​ Previous EMMIR students were financed by (among others): Canada (Student Aid Alberta) Denmark (The Danish State Educational Support, SU) Colombia (COLFUTURO) Germany (BAföG, semester 1, and Auslandsbafög, semester 2, 3 and 4) German government grants and loans (BAföG) are calculated according to the parents' income; therefore not all candidates are eligible to receive it. BAföG is not limited to German citizens (details; only in German), but also available to EU citizens, refugees and stateless persons with permanent residency in Germany. German government grants and loans for studying abroad ('Auslandsbafög', applicable to semester 2 to 4) are available even to candidates who do not receive BAföG in Germany. Please use online translation services (available for free e.g. Google Translate extension in Google Chrome to translate a page) to access the partly German only content of the website – the EMMIR team is unable to provide translation services. Mexico (CONACYT FUNED) Norway (Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund) Spain (ERASMUS+ Master Loan) ​ There are manifold opportunities to apply for third party grants. Click here for an overview offered by the University of Oldenburg. A list of grants available to students of the University of Oldenburg (which you are as an EMMIR student) can be found here: UOL scholarships. As a self-paying student you are eligible to apply for Erasmus+ mobility funds to support your mobility path. Please note however these grants will only be accessible to you once you have started EMMIR and that none of these covers your full monthly expenses. If you need a student visa to enter Germany, non-fee paying (NF) and fee paying (FP) students will have to pay 11,208€ in a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) for their first year living expenses. Please do not apply as NF or FP student if you do not have access to this amount. ​​ ​ Cost of Living The information below is useful to both scholarship and self-funded students who will need an idea of how to finance their stay in Europe/Africa/Asia. ​ Please note that this information refers specifically to the cost of living in various countries, and does not refer to any visa-related expenses. Some countries, such as Germany, may require you to deposit a certain amount of money into a blocked account in order to receive your student visa. For more information on applying for visas, please see the Next Steps page. Oldenburg/Germany: 992 (minimum) up to 1000 Euros/month The cost of living in Germany is relatively high. However, there are many ways for students to reduce their costs: student dormitories and shared flats offer affordable housing, cheap super markets and pubs catering to students are also helpful. Cultural events, sports centres, as well as public transport even certain shops, offer student discounts. Estimations of living costs (incl. accommodation, food, leisure, etc.) in Germany vary between 992 and 1000 Euros per month. Find more detailed information on the website of the German Studentenwerk. 992 Euros per month is the minimum amount required in your bank account to be eligible for a study visa and subsequent residence permit (for non-scholarship students). Stavanger, Norway: about 1200 Euros/month Norway is one of the most expensive countries in the world and it takes a while getting used to the high cost of living. As a student you will need a minimum of approximately 12500 NOK (about 1150 Euros) per month in order to cover basic expenses. However, as a student you can access discounts and significantly reduce your expenses. Manage your budget well and you can enjoy a wide range of activities. Follow this link to find information on average prices in Stavanger. Nova Gorica, Slovenia: about 750 Euros/month The cost of living in Slovenia is relatively low compared to that of Germany or Norway. Prices are highest in Ljubljana, in Nova Gorica students need an average of 750 Euro per month to get along. Prague, Czech Republic: 900 to 1200 Euros/month The Czech Republic is one of the cheaper European countries in the partnership, you will need 900 to 1200 Euro per month to get along. Find out more about student life in the Czech Republic on this website. Accra, Ghana: about 700 to 1000 Euros/month The approximate costs for living expenses per month around Ghana's capital sum up to around 700 to 1000 Euros per month. The monthly rent for a single room on campus is around 120 Euro including utilities. All other living expenses should not exceed 10-12 Euro per day. Kolkata, India: about 500 Euros/month The cost of living in Kolkata is around 500 euros per month including rent, check out this link for more information about prices in Kolkata. ​ Working while studying Working while participating in the EMMIR programme can offer students valuable financial support and a deeper immersion into life in their host countries, though it's important to manage expectations. Many EMMIR students find employment relatively easily through local job centres or platforms like StudIP, with options available in Oldenburg and other partner institutions. However, the jobs students often secure are not the office or research roles they may hope for but are instead more physically demanding positions in factories, warehouses, or other labor-intensive environments. Additionally, students must be mindful of visa restrictions that limit working hours and ensure they comply with local regulations. ​ Employment opportunities may not come in the first semester, when the workload is particularly intensive, but many students find jobs in their third or fourth semester. Beyond Oldenburg, students have taken up a variety of roles in cities like Stavanger, including babysitting, offering city tours, or doing freelance work remotely. Alumni are a great resource for advice on managing the balance between work and study, so students are encouraged to reach out to the EMMIR network for support. ​ Read some insights from students and alumni about their experience working during EMMIR here. ​ ​ Last page update: September 2026

Read more Background & ObjectivesData drives the world, and in recent years, we have witnessed how data has become the primary engine of the Artificial Intelligence revolution. The huge impact of data-driven initiatives in the current economy cannot be questioned, and the European Data Market Study 2024–2026 confirms that data is rapidly becoming the lifeblood of the global economy. Despite the growing impact of AI, the number of skilled data engineers capable of handling complex data-driven AI projects remains very limited. DEAI is world-class excellence programme in the fields of Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, with a strong focus on research and innovation. It aims to become a global leader in the development of knowledge, talent, and leadership to address the productivity gap in complex, large-scale data-driven AI projects. Presentation & StructureThe programme favours the integration of students into a network of specialists and researchers in data engineering and artificial intelligence. The curriculum is jointly delivered by Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB) in Belgium, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) in Spain, Technische Universität Wien (TUW) in Austria, Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 (UCBL) in France and Università degli Studi di Padova (UniPD) in Italy. Scholars from academic partners around the world and partners from leading industries, private R&D companies, service companies, public research institutes, and public authorities will contribute to the programme by training students, providing computers, software, course material, job placement or internship perspectives, as well as financial support. This consortium will prepare the graduates not only to answer today’s professional challenges through a strong connection with the needs coming from the industry, but also to pursue their studies into doctoral programs, through strong connections with the researchers’ and innovators’ views. The master is divided into four semesters of 30 ECTS each. In the first two semesters, students acquire at ULB and UPC fundamentals on data management, data analytics and artificial intelligence. The ULB semester introduces to basic concepts and aims at homogenizing the inherent heterogeneous students’ background, while UPC semester builds on top of that and deepens on fundamental concepts. Then, students participate in the Summer School organised by one of the main or associated partners, introducing them to emerging perspectives in these domains. They can also participate in the Summer of Code, organised in a distributed way by all the partners, which introduces innovation and real-world large-scale training. Students choose for the third semester a specialisation at one of the three other main partners, namely, Knowledge-Driven Data Management and Intelligence at TUW, Business, Economics, and Financial Data Science at UniPd, and Data and Intelligence for Heterogeneous Systems at UCB. Finally, in the fourth semester, students carry out the master’s thesis at any of the main or associated partners. Given the variety of associated partners, through their Master’s Thesis, students can choose among a wide range of future career perspectives, from start-up creation, through consultancy and R&D in industry, to academic research and continuation in a doctoral programme. The tuition language is English. The programme targets students with a Bachelor of Science (or a level equivalent to 180 ETCS) with a major in Computer Science, as well as an English proficiency corresponding to level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. sourceFacts.programme1: EDISS brings together software engineering educators working in data collection, data-driven assessment, and decision-making for both design- and runtime and software engineers, architects and data scientists working on data pipelines, data architectures, DataOps and in experimentation systems. Such synergy leads to sharing knowledge and expertise, and thus creates new ideas and impactful solutions. EDISS will educate experts who can masterfully integrate data science and ML solutions into software and system engineering processes. Programme Design EDISS is a two-year programme (120 ECTS) based on the collaboration between four university partners. Åbo Akademi University is the entry university for all students and in the second year the students will follow their individual mobility path within one of the three specializations provided by EDISS. For each student the choice of the second year institution will be decided, in the second semester of the first year, by the EDISS selection committee based on the student’s list of preferences, his or her academic performance and the teaching staff input. All students completing the EDISS programme will obtain a double master’s degree from Åbo Akademi University and the institution chosen for the second-year specialization. In addition to the mandatory and elective courses offered in the programme, EDISS students will participate in a one-week winter school organized each year during the second semester of the academic year. The programme also includes a mandatory internship for first-year students with an associate company. Study mobility requirements Mobility periods cannot be replaced by virtual mobility (distance learning), which implies physical presence of the students is required during the entire Master programme. In addition, they cannot take place in institutions outside the EMJMD consortium (i.e. partners and/or associated partners). All students must successfully complete a minimum of 30 ECTS in two countries which are different from the country in which you resided at the time of application. sourceFacts.programme1: See water from space.Create solutions on the ground. MSc WAVES - Water Vulnerability Engineering in Spatial Sciences. Two years, three European universities, and one joint programme. Earth observation, hydrological modelling, machine learning, nature-based engineering, and water governance in a single integrated curriculum. The degree in four lines Award: Double MSc Degree, 120 ECTS Duration: Two years, four semesters Mobility: Two countries, plus optional research visitApplication fee: None, ever Start your application Application deadline 15 January 2027 (23:59 CET)No fee to apply · Save and return at any time ·Estimated total cost for self-funded students 120 ECTS over two years One joint programme, double MSc degree. 3 Specialisation tracks Spatial Water Sciences Water Vulnerability Engineering Governance and Policy 8 Countries in the network Netherlands, Italy and Slovenia, plus associated partners in Denmark, Brazil, India, South Africa and Sweden. 3× Co-supervised thesis Every thesis is supervised by at least three partner institutions. WAVES Introduction movie Choose your path Three tracks, one shared concept Students embark on their chosen specialisation from the outset of the programme, following a tailored curriculum and a mobility pathway designed to strengthen their academic and professional expertise in the field. Spatial Water Sciences Measure water from orbit. Model it at basin scale. Satellite hydrology, geostatistics and machine learning across the full water cycle. Year 1: Padova · Year 2: Twente See the modules → Water Vulnerability Engineering Design the defences and quantify what they are worth. River and coastal engineering, geotechnics, nature-based solutions and multi-hazard risk. Year 1: Ljubljana· Year 2: Padova See the modules → Spatial Water Governance and Policy Turn evidence into decisions people accept. Water law, transboundary governance, participatory planning and WASH, on the same quantitative core. Year 1: Ljubljana · Year 2: Twente See the modules → Where WAVES works A genuinely global network. Water vulnerability is not an European problem with an European solution. The consortium teaches across three European campuses and tests what it teaches in catchments on four continents, from the Vecht and the Brenta to the Berg, the Yamuna and the Itajaí. Meet the consortium Fieldwork and Internship Not applying for an EU scholarship? Self-funded and nationally sponsored candidates are welcome and are assessed on exactly the same academic criteria. If you hold, or intend to apply for, funding from Fulbright, DAAD, a Gulf ministry, a Canadian provincial scheme, Australian OS-HELP or your employer, we will issue the conditional admission letter your sponsor needs. sourceFacts.fundingTerms1: Fees and funding There is never a fee to apply, and your ability to pay plays no part in the academic assessment. Below: the Erasmus Mundus scholarship, and the national routes our self-funded applicants most often use. Erasmus Mundus Joint Master ScholarshipFull scholarship, funded by the European Union The scholarship runs for the full 24 months. It pays your tuition and participation costs in full, including the health and accident insurance the consortium arranges for you. You also receive a contribution to field work, and a monthly allowance of €1,400 for living costs. Open to applicants of any nationality. There are 18 scholarships available for the 2027 intake. Deadline. The scholarship and the self-funded rounds close on the 15 of January. Applying for a scholarship and being unsuccessful does not exclude you from a self-funded place. Estimated total cost for self-funded students. Self-funded students pay a tuition fee of €3,000 per year (EU/EEA nationals) or €12,000 per year (non-EU nationals). They also cover their own housing, health insurance, residence permits and travel between the host cities. The host universities give indicative living costs of about €1,300 per month in Enschede, €900–1,000 in Padova and at least €700 in Ljubljana. Across the 24-month programme this averages roughly €1,000 per month, or about €24,000 in total. A self-funded student should therefore plan for about €30,000 (EU/EEA) or €48,000 (non-EU) for the full two-year programme. On top of that, allow about €1,500–2,500 for one-off costs such as housing deposits, residence permits and relocation between countries. These figures are only a guide. Your actual costs depend on your mobility track, your choice of housing and your lifestyle. National and sponsor funding routes The consortium does not administer these schemes and cannot influence their decisions. What we do is issue the conditional admission letter your sponsor needs, normally within ten working days of a decision. Other funding routes Many WAVES students are funded by their government, their employer or a foundation, rather than by an Erasmus Mundus scholarship. The consortium does not run these schemes and has no say in their decisions, but we help you prepare everything your sponsor needs. Government and ministry scholarships. Many ministries of education, water or environment fund master’s study abroad, often in priority fields such as water management and climate adaptation. They usually fund only universities on an approved list. Employer and agency sponsorship. Water authorities, utilities, consultancies and public agencies sometimes sponsor staff for a master’s degree. They often attach a return-of-service agreement. Foundations and development programmes. Private foundations, development banks and international organisations offer scholarships for particular regions or fields. Most have their own deadline, which is often earlier than ours. Student loans. Some national loan schemes can be used abroad, but only at institutions the scheme recognises. Some also require the whole programme to take place in one country. Check four things with your sponsor before you apply Are your universities recognised? Does it fund study in two countries? Does it accept a double-degree programme? Does its timeline fit ours? Budgeting for two years Beyond participation costs, plan for accommodation, health insurance, a residence permit fee and one international move between the first and second year. Costs differ markedly between Enschede, Padova and Ljubljana, and each host university publishes its own indicative figures. Housing Each partner reserves student housing for incoming WAVES students. Applying early matters more than any other single piece of advice on this page. (Cost of living) Insurance and permits Health insurance is compulsory in all three countries. Residence permit fees and processing times differ; the international offices give exact figures on admission. The move between years One relocation is built into the programme. Scholarship holders receive a contribution towards travel and installation; self-funded students should budget for it explicitly. Student voice. Two elected student representatives per cohort sit on the Quality Assurance Committee with full speaking and voting rights, and one attends the Joint Programme Board. Representation is a standing item, not an invitation. Still unsure whether you can afford it? Ask us. We would rather help you find a funding route than lose a strong candidate to a wrong assumption about cost. About the Programme The Joint Master Programme in Marine Biotechnology (JMPMB) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) programme, co-funded by the European Union and delievered within the framework of one of the first transnational European universities. It is an integrated multidisciplinary programme that provides the student with a high-quality academic education, building professional competences in the area of marine biotechnology (also called blue biotechnology) and helping to address its global challenges. It will ensure that students: Essential interdisciplinary training in key topics related to Marine Biotechnology; Opportunities to specialise within one of the four thematical tracks: (1) Innovative Bioproducts for Future; (2) Blue Biomass; (3) Marine Biorefinery; (4) Aquaculture Biotechnology; A tailored study programme according to their aspirations via individual professional practice (internship), individual research (academic research integration) and thesis work. This Marine Biotechnology Masters gives the student multiple travel options within the alliance. Students are integrated into a multicultural study group and a professional network, offering an immersive system of project-based learning in the ‘real world’ economy. The JMPMB is focussed on applications of Marine Biotechnology to the health, cosmetics and agri-food sectors, leading the students through a pipeline on marine biotechnology including: Biochemical and genomic prospecting tools for searching new molecules from aquatic resources. Microorganisms, micro-algae and seaweed biomass production as the feedstock of new compound and. Biochemical and biotechnology tools for extraction and functionalization of new compounds obtained from marine biomass for application to health, cosmetics and agri-food sectors. About the Programme The Joint Master Programme in Marine Biotechnology (JMPMB) is an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) programme, co-funded by the European Union and delievered within the framework of one of the first transnational European universities. It is an integrated multidisciplinary programme that provides the student with a high-quality academic education, building professional competences in the area of marine biotechnology (also called blue biotechnology) and helping to address its global challenges. It will ensure that students: Essential interdisciplinary training in key topics related to Marine Biotechnology; Opportunities to specialise within one of the four thematical tracks: (1) Innovative Bioproducts for Future; (2) Blue Biomass; (3) Marine Biorefinery; (4) Aquaculture Biotechnology; A tailored study programme according to their aspirations via individual professional practice (internship), individual research (academic research integration) and thesis work. This Marine Biotechnology Masters gives the student multiple travel options within the alliance. Students are integrated into a multicultural study group and a professional network, offering an immersive system of project-based learning in the ‘real world’ economy. The JMPMB is focussed on applications of Marine Biotechnology to the health, cosmetics and agri-food sectors, leading the students through a pipeline on marine biotechnology including: Biochemical and genomic prospecting tools for searching new molecules from aquatic resources. Microorganisms, micro-algae and seaweed biomass production as the feedstock of new compound and. Biochemical and biotechnology tools for extraction and functionalization of new compounds obtained from marine biomass for application to health, cosmetics and agri-food sectors.
